name: _grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback
description: Representative ATen signature (not exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::_grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback(Tensor input, Tensor grid, int interpolation_mode, int padding_mode, bool align_corners) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract, defining and exercising the overloads, keyword arguments, return values, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior; do not narrow tests to this signature, remove workload rows, or adapt reference semantics to fit it. All registered schemas from the supplied evidence, verbatim: (1) aten::_grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback(Tensor input, Tensor grid, int interpolation_mode, int padding_mode, bool align_corners) -> Tensor; (2) aten::_grid_sampler_2d_cpu_fallback.out(Tensor input, Tensor grid, int interpolation_mode, int padding_mode, bool align_corners, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics derived from the tests: a CompositeExplicitAutograd 2-D grid-sampling composite whose body hardcodes float32 and reads host memory, so its real contract is CPU + float32 + rank 4. input is an (N, C, H, W) image and grid is (N, OH, OW, 2) with grid.size(0) == input.size(0) and grid.size(-1) == 2; the result is (N, C, OH, OW) and the default overload is out of place (operands are not touched). interpolation_mode selects bilinear=0 / nearest=1 / bicubic=2, padding_mode selects zeros=0 / border=1 / reflection=2, and align_corners is a bool that changes coordinate normalization; out-of-range mode values are accepted natively (the scalar loop falls through to bilinear/zeros), so no invalid-mode negative case exists. autograd through the composite is defined and backward gradients for input and grid are compared. Invalid ranks (input rank 3/5, grid rank 3), grid last-dim != 2, batch mismatch, empty input height/width and non-float32 dtypes raise RuntimeError/TypeError and remain asserted in pytest rather than encoded here. Overload-dependent behavior not expressible by this model: only the .out overload is in place, mutating the keyword-only `out` parameter and returning that same buffer as an alias of it, and it resizes a mismatched buffer with a deprecation warning; `out` is keyword-only and required for that overload. This definition models only the representative `default` overload; the .out overload and all error, alias and mutation behavior stay with the original Gems pytest.
